app_info.subtitle: Verifiable memory of the physical world
app_info.description: emem is a shared, verifiable memory of the physical world for AI. Every place resolves to one canonical address, every observation about it becomes one signed fact you can verify offline, and every fact has a short citation token that resolves anywhere to the byte-identical signed value. Ask about a place (elevation, vegetation, surface water, built-up context, flood signals), an area (a native-resolution raster field, or a field over time), change over time, or similarity between places; get back cite-able, ed25519-signed receipts. No API key or signup required.

emem_ask.readOnlyHint_justification: Grounds the question against real places and, on a cold cell, auto-materializes and signs new facts (Sentinel-2/-1, Cop-DEM, JRC GSW, Overture, weather) into emem's publicly readable store before answering. Nothing is overwritten or removed, so destructiveHint stays false, but the call can add state that other readers will see and therefore is not read-only.
emem_ask.openWorldHint_justification: This tool resolves real-world place mentions and may fetch upstream Earth-observation data to answer the user's place-based question. It does not create public content or affect external systems. This flag answers MCP's question, which is whether the call may reach an unbounded set of external entities (here: upstream Earth-observation archives), not whether it writes anything. It writes nothing: readOnlyHint is true and destructiveHint is false, and those are the fields that carry 'can this change state someone else can see'. Every tool in this submission is read-only; none of emem's write tools is exposed here.
emem_ask.destructiveHint_justification: This tool is read-only. It does not delete or modify any data.

emem_locate.readOnlyHint_justification: Resolves a place name to coordinates and available bands. No writes.
emem_locate.openWorldHint_justification: This tool resolves free-text place names, addresses, or coordinates against real-world geocoding and emem inventory data. This flag answers MCP's question, which is whether the call may reach an unbounded set of external entities (here: upstream Earth-observation archives), not whether it writes anything. It writes nothing: readOnlyHint is true and destructiveHint is false, and those are the fields that carry 'can this change state someone else can see'. Every tool in this submission is read-only; none of emem's write tools is exposed here.

emem_recall.readOnlyHint_justification: Recall auto-materializes on a miss: if the requested band is not yet held for that cell, the responder fetches it upstream, signs the resulting fact and appends it to the shared store. Append-only, never an overwrite, so destructiveHint stays false.
emem_recall.openWorldHint_justification: This tool can auto-materialize facts from registered Earth-observation data sources when a requested band is missing. This flag answers MCP's question, which is whether the call may reach an unbounded set of external entities (here: upstream Earth-observation archives), not whether it writes anything. It writes nothing: readOnlyHint is true and destructiveHint is false, and those are the fields that carry 'can this change state someone else can see'. Every tool in this submission is read-only; none of emem's write tools is exposed here.

emem_verify_receipt.readOnlyHint_justification: Verifies a signed receipt envelope. No writes.
emem_verify_receipt.openWorldHint_justification: Checks receipt data supplied by the caller without contacting external systems.

emem_memory_token.readOnlyHint_justification: Composes a citation handle from a cell and fact id. No writes.
emem_memory_token.openWorldHint_justification: Formats an address string from data already in hand; contacts nothing.

emem_find_similar.readOnlyHint_justification: Nearest-neighbour search over the Tessera embedding. No writes.
emem_find_similar.openWorldHint_justification: May materialize an embedding for the seed cell from Earth-observation data before the search. This flag answers MCP's question, which is whether the call may reach an unbounded set of external entities (here: upstream Earth-observation archives), not whether it writes anything. It writes nothing: readOnlyHint is true and destructiveHint is false, and those are the fields that carry 'can this change state someone else can see'. Every tool in this submission is read-only; none of emem's write tools is exposed here.

emem_band_raster.readOnlyHint_justification: Rendering a band over a region materializes and signs any cells not already held, so the call can append new facts to the shared store. Append-only.
emem_band_raster.openWorldHint_justification: Reads a Sentinel-2 scene window from open Earth-observation sources to compute the field. This flag answers MCP's question, which is whether the call may reach an unbounded set of external entities (here: upstream Earth-observation archives), not whether it writes anything. It writes nothing: readOnlyHint is true and destructiveHint is false, and those are the fields that carry 'can this change state someone else can see'. Every tool in this submission is read-only; none of emem's write tools is exposed here.
emem_band_raster.destructiveHint_justification: Read-only field derivation; the artifact is content-addressed and immutable.

emem_band_cube.readOnlyHint_justification: Building a field-over-time cube materializes and signs the cells and timeslots not already held. Append-only.
emem_band_cube.openWorldHint_justification: Reads one Sentinel-2 scene per requested date from open Earth-observation sources. This flag answers MCP's question, which is whether the call may reach an unbounded set of external entities (here: upstream Earth-observation archives), not whether it writes anything. It writes nothing: readOnlyHint is true and destructiveHint is false, and those are the fields that carry 'can this change state someone else can see'. Every tool in this submission is read-only; none of emem's write tools is exposed here.
emem_band_cube.destructiveHint_justification: Read-only field-over-time derivation; content-addressed and immutable.

emem_change_attribution.readOnlyHint_justification: Attribution recalls both endpoints of the comparison, which auto-materializes and signs anything missing before the terms can be computed. Append-only.
emem_change_attribution.openWorldHint_justification: May read the cited bands (materializing on a miss) to assemble the evidence ledger. This flag answers MCP's question, which is whether the call may reach an unbounded set of external entities (here: upstream Earth-observation archives), not whether it writes anything. It writes nothing: readOnlyHint is true and destructiveHint is false, and those are the fields that carry 'can this change state someone else can see'. Every tool in this submission is read-only; none of emem's write tools is exposed here.
emem_change_attribution.destructiveHint_justification: Read-only evidence assembly; the numeric split is null by design, nothing is fabricated.

test_cases.prompt: What is the elevation at Helsinki-Vantaa Airport?
test_cases.expected: Returns elevation value with a signed fact CID

test_cases.prompt: Does downtown Miami have flood risk signals?
test_cases.expected: Returns elevation and surface water data with signed receipts

test_cases.prompt: What signed geospatial facts are available for Lake Erie, Ohio?
test_cases.expected: Returns available bands and signed facts for the location

test_cases.prompt: Is New Orleans at risk of flooding based on elevation?
test_cases.expected: Returns low elevation data and surface water recurrence with CIDs

test_cases.prompt: What evidence supports a flood risk assessment for Miami Beach?
test_cases.expected: Returns elevation, surface water, and vegetation data with verifiable receipts

test_cases.prompt: Give me a citation token for the NDVI at this farm that I can re-verify later.
test_cases.expected: Returns an emem:fact: token that resolves to the byte-identical signed fact and verifies offline

test_cases.prompt: I need the 10 m red-band raster over this bounding box, not per-cell numbers.
test_cases.expected: Returns an emem:raster: field token plus a content-addressed grid artifact the caller can re-hash

negative_test_cases.prompt: What is the stock price of Apple?
negative_test_cases.expected: emem tools should not be called. This is not a place-based question.

negative_test_cases.prompt: Write me a poem about the ocean.
negative_test_cases.expected: emem tools should not be called. This is a creative writing request.

negative_test_cases.prompt: How do I install Python on Windows?
negative_test_cases.expected: emem tools should not be called. This is a software question.
